suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Create comprehensive documentation for the trace infrastructure including: event taxonomy (levels, categories, IDs), how to add new events, payload size guidelines, and example emit functions. The trace system (trace.h, trace_types.h, trace_events.def) is complex but undocumented.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: DIAG-001 review found that workers had to reverse-engineer trace patterns. trace_types.h defines categories as powers of 2 (0x01, 0x02, 0x04, etc.) but this taxonomy is not documented. trace_events.def uses TRACE_EVENT macro pattern that requires understanding.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add convention: When documenting analysis findings, use docs/ directory with feature-specific markdown files. DIAG-002 and DIAG-003 both created docs/*.md files, establishing a useful pattern for diagnostic artifacts.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: DIAG-002 created docs/exec_window_analysis.md, DIAG-003 created docs/mm_lifecycle_analysis.md. Both follow consistent structure with Feature ID, Overview, Analysis, and Conclusion sections.

rejectedObservations.observation: DIAG-001 has duplicate trace_emit call at line 52 of task.c
rejectedObservations.reason: This is a minor code quality issue flagged as non-blocking. The duplicate emit doesn't affect correctness, only adds slight noise to traces. Not worth a fix cycle.

rejectedObservations.observation: DIAG-001 trace_emit in inline task_set_mm may impact hot path performance
rejectedObservations.reason: This is a performance consideration, not a correctness issue. The trace system has enable checks that minimize overhead. If performance becomes an issue, a compile-time flag can be added later.

rejectedObservations.observation: DIAG-001 TRACE_EVENT_MM_RELEASE emitted after NULL assignment shows NULL instead of old_mm
rejectedObservations.reason: This is intentional - the trace marks when the window STARTS (after old mm is released). The old_mm value is captured in mm_release's own trace event. Current ordering is semantically correct.

reviewNotes.DIAG-001: Diagnostic logging implementation is well-executed with trace points strategically placed. All 119 tests pass. Minor non-blocking issues around duplicate emits and trace ordering, but no correctness problems.
reviewNotes.DIAG-002: Exec window analysis is comprehensive and accurate. Correctly identifies the mm_release/task_set_mm window vulnerability with four risk scenarios. Recommended fix (Option 1) was implemented in FIX-001.
reviewNotes.DIAG-003: Reference counting analysis covers all 5 relevant source files (mmap.c, init.c, fork.c, exec.c, exit.c). Confirmed exec window vulnerability. Pattern summary table is valuable for future maintenance.
reviewNotes.FIX-001: Fix correctly addresses root cause identified in DIAG-002. Sets current->mm and current->mem to NULL before mm_release(), preventing dangling pointers. All 119 tests pass with no regressions. Well-documented with explanatory comments.
